n: Like a street vendor calling customers, God shouts: everyone who is thirsty, come! Even if you have no money, come take water, wine, and milk for free. Salvation is a gift, not a purchase. Jacob echoes this in 2 Nephi 9:50.
Why spend money on what isn’t real food, and work for what never satisfies? Listen to God and feast on what’s truly good. Many of us spend our lives chasing things that can’t fill us.

f.w: spend money for that which is not bread

n: Listen and come to Me so your soul may live. God offers an everlasting covenant—the faithful love promised to David. Paul connects the “sure mercies of David” to Christ’s resurrection.
God made David—and ultimately David’s greater descendant, the Messiah—a witness, leader, and commander for the nations.
Israel will call nations it didn’t know, and they will run to it because of the Lord who has glorified His people—missionary work across the world.

f.w: nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee

n: Seek the Lord while He can be found; call on Him while He is near. There is urgency—don’t put off turning to God.

f.w: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found

n: Let the wicked abandon their ways and even their thoughts, and return to the Lord. He will have mercy and pardon generously. Repentance changes both actions and thinking.
God’s thoughts and ways are not like ours. Even His forgiveness is beyond what we would expect or give.

f.w: my thoughts are not your thoughts

n: As high as the sky is above the earth, so much higher are God’s ways and thoughts. Trusting Him means accepting that He sees far more than we do.

f.w: as the heavens are higher than the earth

n: Rain and snow don’t return to the sky without first watering the ground, making plants grow, and providing seed and bread.
Just so, God’s word never comes back empty. It always accomplishes His purpose. His promises will be fulfilled.

f.w: it shall not return unto me void

n: God’s people will leave captivity with joy and be led home in peace; mountains will sing and trees clap their hands. All creation celebrates redemption.

f.w: all the trees of the field shall clap their hands
ye shall go out with joy

n: Thorns and briers—symbols of the curse on the ground after the Fall—will be replaced by cypress and myrtle. This renewed land will be a lasting monument to the Lord’s name.

f.w: Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree

f.g: A fragrant evergreen shrub, a symbol of joy and peace.
